title: How the Madisonville boat job worked
summary: The band played sets on the hour-long trip across the lake from West End; they cannot recall whether they stayed overnight.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: What was it like working on the Madisonville? How did that gig work?

Oh it was, you played, when the boat was going over, you played several sets. He played mostly to, I guess, to break the monotonous of the trip because that was the only way you could get across the lake at that time. And they played mostly to break the monotonous of the trip I guess because it was the only way you could get across the lake. He used to hold automobiles and picnic parties and so forth. He would leave from West End and go to Mandeville and Madisonville. But it wasn't a spectacular job, it was just a music job is all I can see. Because you'd play a few minutes and then you'd rest and a few minutes, because the trip took about, oh I guess about an hour and something across the lake.
Well what about it? Did you stay over there all night?
Well no, we would, I don't quite remember, did we stay over there all night?
Yeah, we'd stay over there, the weekend. Couldn't even see, we was waiting three nights or all that. I wouldn't go down there. I can't even remember.
See, couldn't even have the crossway or nothing then, because it was day and night.

I don't remember if the boat stayed in Madisonville or whether we played that evening trip, two o'clock, I know we'd leave about two o'clock. It was the whole season. And I don't know whether we came back that night or not. I don't remember. I'll be frank with you, I can't remember.
